title: Mount shared views and couple capture to displayed state
description: Integrate SharedViewDocument into the Canvas runtime, surfaces, control socket and MCP so an agent and human operate on the same mounted view. Image/PDF viewports and attention must render visibly; captures must identify and use the exact displayed view revision and source positions.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas can open and inspect a shared image view, atomically patch its viewport/attention, visibly render the result, and capture the same view revision; human pan/zoom updates the document; MCP schemas and receipts expose exact view and source revisions; tests reject stale or mismatched capture requests.
notes:
2026-09-08 slice: image/PDF loads now mount SharedViewDocument state; control/MCP inspect exposes visible absolute surface bounds and exact view/source revisions; canvas_view_patch visibly applies normalized GPU crop and attention; canvas_view_capture validates runtime+view revisions, captures only the resolved surface, returns metadata+PNG, and re-inspects after readback to reject concurrent changes. Generic surface screenshots now use surface bounds. Full workspace build/test/clippy/fmt passed. Remaining before close: direct human pan/zoom must mutate the same view. Display-independent offscreen/headless GPU capture is tracked by dock-cov.12.
Live macOS smoke testing exposed a compositor false positive: screencapture returned bare wallpaper while runtime state still identified the requested surface. Surface capture now verifies the existing Canvas traffic-light chrome using runtime theme colors and fails loudly when pixels are occluded or come from another Space. MCP capture remains passive and never shows, focuses, or rearranges Canvas. Reliable occlusion-independent capture remains dock-cov.12.
Direct local MCP setup verified 2026-09-08: installed matching dock-canvas/dock-canvas-mcp binaries without launching or focusing Canvas, retained the FPL Desktop Bridge dock-canvas connector, registered ~/.local/bin/dock-canvas-mcp globally in Codex as dock-canvas, negotiated MCP 2025-06-18, listed all 15 tools, and completed a read-only canvas_inspect call.
Live direct MCP joyride: relaunched the matching runtime, opened docs/screenshots/dock-dark.png as joyride-dock on the right display, inspected its exact bounds and SharedViewDocument revision, then patched viewport plus agent attention from view revision 1 to 2 with a successful revisioned receipt. macOS screencapture still omits the on-screen Metal host window and returns the pixels beneath it; the capture guard correctly rejects the result. Canvas windows now opt into CanJoinAllSpaces, FullScreenAuxiliary, and Stationary, reapplied on explicit focus after native registration. Offscreen GPU capture remains the reliable readback path in dock-cov.12.

title: Define joint artifact and view-state contract
description: Specify and implement the versioned boundary that lets Canvas, a human, and an agent refer to the same visual thing and the same exact view of it. Cover finite artifacts and live sources without coupling the document to SSE, inbox, filesystem, camera, or model-provider details.
design: Model source identity/provenance separately from ViewState. A view owns normalized viewport, optional selection/annotation, page or playhead, filters and source revision. All mutations use optimistic revisions. Capture/inspection must name the resulting view revision so an agent cannot silently inspect pixels different from what Canvas shows.
acceptance_criteria: Rust types validate source references, provenance and bounded shared view state; patches can focus a normalized image region without replacing the artifact; serialization is MCP-schema-compatible; tests cover invalid bounds, stale revisions and a finite image plus a live graph source; the architecture document gives a manual runbook from source resolution to shared display and inspection.
notes: Implemented dock_canvas::view contract with keyed multi-source bindings, artifact/live source positions, normalized viewport, visible attention ownership, page/timeline navigation, typed parameters, and atomic revision-checked patches. Tests prove image-region focus preserves artifact identity, two live sources share one view lifecycle, invalid regions/source modes fail, stale patches conflict, and JSON round-trips. Added architecture boundary and manual runbook; repaired existing all-feature mlua callback/table integration exposed by the gate.
close_reason: The shared multi-source artifact/view-state contract, validation, patch semantics, tests, architecture document, and runbook are implemented.

title: Make Canvas the shared human-agent visualization plane
description: Canvas is the common visualization layer for static artifacts and live data, and the joint visual context shared by a human and AI. Any authorized source can publish typed data or references; deterministic reducers and capability-scoped Lua map them into views; both parties observe and change the same revisioned view state instead of maintaining separate chat and screen representations.
design: Separate immutable or owner-referenced artifacts from mutable joint view state. Normalize finite snapshots and unbounded streams behind one typed source contract. Keep transport, authorization, decoding and rendering outside Lua; Lua adapts bounded typed inputs into retained visual scenes. MCP expresses intent and reads exact state; the owner-local socket applies deterministic revisioned transitions. View state includes viewport, selection, page/playhead, filters, presentation and provenance so agent inspection is visibly mirrored on Canvas.
acceptance_criteria: An agent can publish or resolve an artifact/data source, open a shared view, focus or annotate the exact region it is inspecting, and capture that same view revision; human interactions update the state the agent reads; one streaming source and one finite artifact use the same lifecycle; a Lua adapter can render a bounded unfamiliar graph stream without owning I/O; provenance and authorization remain inspectable.
notes: 2026-09-08 product direction: Canvas is the shared view/window manager for human-AI collaboration and the common view language for all signals. Reference workloads include Elmer's brain and MCP firing SSE graphs, Edgerunner DAGs, Prometheus instruments, Panopticon maps, trading/mixed-export analysis, presence, terminals/NVR/media, STL/STEP/wireframe/FEA/CAM/microscope, Gaussian splats/RuView/PolyLayout, music visualizers, generated CSV+Lua/template explanations, Maxim-style narratives and future XR. Preserve steering/observability and hands-on engineering/vibe-coding as equal modes. Alfalfa owns identity/workflow/admin; JARVIS owns voice/presence; domain systems own data/actions/hardware; Canvas owns shared views/layout/capture/presentation. Portable state uses compact JSON snapshots plus JSONL patch/receipt journals; Lua owns bounded presentation logic.

title: Configure Canvas overlays and global visibility
description: The shared multi-display Canvas currently repeats overlays per host window, the compact presence indicator does not provide JARVIS's working live tray behavior, and there is no global way to reveal the underlying macOS desktop. Add deterministic display anchors for overlays, place the live presence rail on the bottom-left/leftmost selected display, place the Conky HUD on the rightmost selected display, preserve Lua as a client of the runtime configuration interface, and register a global Mac shortcut that atomically shows or hides every Canvas host window.
acceptance_criteria: Presence rail updates live and renders only on the leftmost selected display; Conky HUD renders only on the rightmost selected display; socket state/configuration represents overlay anchors without duplicating placement logic in Lua; a documented global Mac shortcut hides and restores all selected Canvas windows together; tests cover viewport anchors and visibility state transitions; live three-monitor verification succeeds.
notes: 2026-09-08 implemented and deployed: typed OverlaySettings via raw socket and MCP; defaults place live JARVIS rail/preview on leftmost, HUD on rightmost, FPL mark leftmost, compact orb hidden, shortcut help centered. Ctrl-Option-C globally hides/restores all native Canvas windows while retaining daemon state; Ctrl-Option-? globally opens Help; plain ? opens Help only after a Canvas background click; Ctrl-Up/Down cycles exact project workspaces; Ctrl-Option-J toggles JARVIS presentation. Rebuilt the existing JARVIS Presence app after its packaged binary had been cleaned, restarted its owner LaunchAgent, and proved current presence reaches Canvas. Live proof: three selected 1920x1200 displays, shared 5760x1200 frame, static aurora-drift speed 0, visibility false then true, shortcut_help shown, presence live. Full workspace build/test/strict Clippy/format pass.
close_reason: Overlay placement, live presence restoration, shortcut help, and global three-window visibility toggle are implemented, tested, deployed, and live-verified.

title: Present Canvas as one shared desktop across displays
description: A single oversized native Canvas window records a multi-display frame but macOS separate Spaces prevents reliable presentation across the physical displays. Present one host window per selected display while retaining one WorkspaceDocument, one global z-order, and one virtual coordinate space so surfaces can be dragged across seams.
design: Add a renderer-neutral display topology and virtual-to-local projection boundary. The shell owns one borderless window per display and renders/clips the shared document through each display viewport. Pointer events translate from host-window local coordinates into virtual desktop coordinates before using the existing interaction engine. Monitor assignment remains host-local and socket/MCP driven.
acceptance_criteria: On the current three-display Mac, Canvas visibly covers each selected display; a surface can be dragged across both seams while preserving size, focus, and z-order; disconnect/reconnect and nonzero/negative origins fail or reconcile deterministically; socket inspection exposes selected display targets; tests cover topology, projection, and cross-display pointer translation.
notes: 2026-09-08 shared desktop slice implemented: one native host window per selected display over one WorkspaceDocument/global z-order/virtual frame; window-local pointer coordinates project to shared coordinates; display target exposed through socket and Canvas MCP; tests cover negative origins, seam projection, topology validation and second-display pointer translation. Live three-display 5760x1200 presentation verified by user and visibility hotkey proof. Remaining before closing: respond to display topology changes at runtime and prove disconnect/reconnect reconciliation without restarting Canvas.

title: Materialize and recover the managed Canvas native window
description: The managed dock-canvas process can own its socket, restore its full project WorkspaceDocument, and report connected displays while macOS exposes no native window. Focus is then a no-op because App.window remains unset. Closing or relaunching must recreate the desktop presentation instead of leaving a headless control process.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh LaunchAgent start creates one borderless Canvas window on the resolved display target; closing or losing that window either recreates it or terminates the runtime so supervision restarts it; focus brings it to the active Space; inspect distinguishes document state from presentation-window state; a live screenshot proves the restored Dock project desktop is visible after restart.
notes: 2026-09-07 slice cfdd1a0 replaces implicit oldest-window lookup with an explicit iced daemon window open, retains the exact returned window ID, and tests persistent borderless desktop settings. Deployed LaunchAgent restores dock with surfaces=1 and CoreGraphics proves one on-screen 1920x1200 window at 3840,0. Remaining: sharing state is still 0, so screencapture omits Canvas; inspect must report window presentation state and close/recovery needs a live proof.

title: Stop Canvas background flicker and expose frame pacing
description: The animated Canvas background flickers severely in the live desktop. Make shader animation opt-in while unstable, schedule generation at a bounded cadence, measure generated/presented cadence over a rolling interval, and expose a small configurable FPS diagnostic so frame pacing can be verified before deployment.
design: Keep timing deterministic in the Canvas runtime. Separate tick cadence, expensive shader generation cadence, and diagnostic sampling. Do not perform synchronous GPU readback unless animated background state explicitly enables it.
acceptance_criteria: The default Canvas launch is visually stable. Shader frames are never generated faster than the configured cap. A socket-controlled FPS overlay reports measured cadence. Tests cover disabled/default scheduling, capped scheduling, and meter calculation. The live right-monitor instance is verified without flicker.
notes: Implemented 2026-09-07: replaced synchronous wgpu readback plus per-frame iced image-handle allocation with an iced-native retained GPU shader primitive. Screensaver state is explicit over the socket, defaults disabled, validates 1-60 FPS, and optionally shows measured/target FPS. A deadline-based FrameClock bounds updates without accumulating timer drift. Live managed binary on right display measures 15.01 FPS at a 15 FPS target, CPU ~8%, RSS held 77.7-77.9 MiB over 10 seconds. Found and killed unmanaged target/debug processes that were stealing the socket from the LaunchAgent. 76 Canvas tests pass and strict all-target Clippy passes. Awaiting subjective confirmation that the display is visually calm before closing.
close_reason: Replaced the flickering readback path with retained GPU rendering, removed per-frame image allocation, added bounded deterministic pacing and optional FPS diagnostics, added compile-time WGSL parsing, eliminated duplicate unmanaged runtimes, and verified the managed right-display instance at ~15 FPS with stable RSS.

title: Render Panopticon intelligence as a native Canvas map
description: Add a first-class renderer-neutral map surface and native Canvas adapter. Canvas owns camera state, map interaction, transition timing, reduced-motion behavior, and compositing; it consumes authorized opaque map resources and never stores credentials or asks Panopticon to dictate pixels. Resolve natural-language place names outside the renderer into exact versioned geographic extents, then apply deterministic camera intents. Use a proven map engine through an offscreen texture boundary rather than implementing tile layout, labels, collision, and camera flight from scratch.
design: Define maps.viewport.v1 with target variants extent, center_zoom, entity, and current_results; WGS84 antimeridian-safe bounds; padding; bearing/pitch; and a renderer hint transition of jump, ease, or fly with bounded duration. Derive center/zoom from extent plus actual surface size instead of storing redundant values. Add a Map surface/resource binding to the WorkspaceDocument and revisioned patch protocol. Prototype MapLibre Native FFI owned-texture or borrowed-texture compositing on macOS Metal, keeping network/tile parsing off the iced render thread. The MCP path accepts an already-resolved extent or stable place reference; an orchestrator may resolve a phrase through Panopticon before issuing one exact Canvas mutation. Ambiguity must return candidates, never silently choose Springfield/Fremont. Preserve human gestures and cancel/retarget an in-flight agent animation deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: From one MCP-driven request, Canvas can show and smoothly fly between world, Seattle, Fremont Seattle, Manhattan, the five boroughs, and the NY/NJ/CT tri-state extent; fit current query results; and follow an entity. Camera movement is smooth on reference hardware, interruptible by direct human input, honors reduced motion, and does not mutate the durable document every frame. Retina output is sharp, labels do not visibly reflow after settling, stale tile/data failures are explicit, and credentials/endpoints never appear in the document or MCP receipt. Unit tests cover extent fitting, antimeridian bounds, ambiguity, revision conflicts, duration bounds, and transition cancellation; a live visual test records frame-time and command-to-first-motion latency.
notes:
Backend-first slice implemented locally without selecting a permanent engine: added a generic typed VisualBackend lifecycle with shared mount/update/resize/input/event/render/suspend/unmount semantics, revision enforcement, reduced-motion context, retained-frame outcomes, and adapter-neutral errors. Added maps.viewport model types with opaque resource identity, semantic layers, extent/center/follow/fit targets, antimeridian-safe bounds, provenance refs, surface-derived Web Mercator camera fitting, bounded jump/ease/fly transitions, and reduced-motion resolution. Validation on 2026-09-07 used /Volumes/DOC MOVIES/dock-cargo-target because the local disk filled: all 48 dock-canvas all-feature library tests pass and strict all-feature library Clippy with -D warnings passes. Focused rustfmt is clean. Concurrent Canvas work remains in the shared worktree and was preserved. Remaining on this feature: put MapSurface into the WorkspaceDocument after current document work settles, implement the MapLibre FFI texture adapter behind VisualBackend, wire map gestures/animation interruption, add map-specific MCP convenience operations, and perform native visual/performance proof.
2026-09-07 renderer direction: native-first Rust + Lua + wgpu/WGSL. Do not introduce deck.gl or a large JavaScript visualization runtime. MapLibre Native may remain a bounded C++/FFI map backend behind VisualBackend; Canvas owns the Rust compositor and MCP surface. Treat browser rendering as a thin fallback or a build from the shared typed scene contract, not the source of truth.

title: Add direct mouse interaction and drag placement to Canvas
description: Build the renderer-neutral Canvas interaction engine needed for immediate direct manipulation: hit testing, pointer capture, click-to-focus, drag-to-move, resize handles, z-order promotion, and predictable edge/grid snapping. The iced shell will translate native mouse events into this engine and apply validated workspace patches so agents and humans share the same placement model.
design: Keep input normalization and interaction state in dock-canvas library. Renderers supply logical pointer events and current surface geometry. The engine returns deterministic intents; the authoritative workspace/runtime validates and applies them. No OS mouse injection or Accessibility permission belongs here.
acceptance_criteria: Focused tests cover hit order, click focus, captured drags outside original bounds, move and resize constraints, release/cancel, and deterministic snapping; interaction state emits typed intents/patches without owning renderer or OS state; integration points are documented for iced, touch, and later XR pointers.
notes:
Implemented renderer-neutral direct manipulation in crates/dock-canvas/src/interaction.rs with normalized logical pointer events, ordered z-aware hit testing, eight resize handles, focus/front promotion, pointer capture, move/resize bounds intents, release/cancel restoration, workspace/minimum-size constraints, and stable edge-before-grid snap tie-breaking. Module docs define iced, touch, and XR adapter boundaries. Focused validation passed in isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Volumes/DOC MOVIES/dock-agent-interaction: 6 interaction tests and cargo clippy -p dock-canvas --lib -- -D warnings.
Live macOS proof completed: converted the running two-surface workspace to Canvas layout and injected a real pointer drag over mmd-diagram. Bounds moved from x=0.70,y=0.48 to x=0.6375,y=0.41148937; focus changed to mmd-diagram; z layer promoted from 1 to 3; authoritative document revision advanced. Runtime remained live on the right display.
close_reason: Interaction engine and focused coverage complete; iced integration remains with the parent Canvas shell work.

title: Make Coherence the native Canvas style owner
description: Canvas currently consumes a reduced Coherence color palette but hardcodes most iced component recipes: typography sizes, spacing, radii, opacity, elevation, window chrome, instrument panels, tables, charts, meters, focus and hover. Promote the native renderer boundary so Coherence owns semantic visual tokens and reusable iced style/component functions while Canvas owns layout, data, interaction, and workspace state.
design: Do not parse browser CSS inside iced and do not introduce a general styling language. Keep Coherence's current CSS custom properties as the canonical token source; extend its bounded exporter to generate complete Rust tokens. Define a small shared component contract—role, variant, interaction state, density and size class—with CSS and coherence-iced implementations both owned and parity-tested in Coherence. Theme data remains project-scoped and serializable; Lua receives read-only semantic tokens and selects declared variants but cannot invent ambient styling or own rendering. Commit Coherence first, then sync a pinned checksummed snapshot into Dock; do not copy component recipes into Dock.
acceptance_criteria: A committed and versioned coherence-iced artifact is synced into Dock with provenance; Dock no longer projects Coherence into a lossy color-only ThemePalette for native components; semantic typography, full spacing/radius/density, surface layers, focus, opacity/elevation and data-viz roles reach iced; Canvas chrome and dock-widgets use shared Coherence recipes; light/dark/project/imported palette modes render legibly; visual fixtures and keyboard focus states are verified; consumer sync detects drift.
notes: Audit 2026-09-08: Dock's vendored coherence-tokens snapshot exposes upstream colors/spacing/radii but ThemePalette keeps only 13 colors and ThemeMetrics keeps four spaces, one radius and two font sizes. dock-widgets::live accepts only ThemePalette and hardcodes panel padding 16, radius 7, alpha 0.72, type sizes, shadow and graph treatments; Canvas independently hardcodes chrome/dock/HUD styles. Local Coherence has an uncommitted coherence-iced draft with theme/button/input/select/divider/action/account-row functions and richer Precise tokens. Preserve that work, commit it upstream, add Canvas/data-viz recipes there, then sync through scripts/sync-components.mjs with provenance.

title: Add display toggles and screen-aware surface placement
description: Canvas needs deterministic left/center/right display control for humans and agents. Add Ctrl-1/Ctrl-2/Ctrl-3 to toggle individual displays, Ctrl-0 to show Canvas on all displays, ordinal display targeting over MCP/socket, and a placement helper that can put a surface in a named region of a chosen display while preserving work on other screens.
design: Keep display topology and region-to-normalized-layout conversion in dock-canvas. MCP expresses intent using one-based display ordinals and stable surface IDs; the owner-local runtime resolves current geometry and emits exact state transitions. Preserve unrelated surface placements and expose resulting state in receipts/inspection.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl-0 through Ctrl-3 operate on displays ordered left-to-right; non-contiguous selections such as displays 1 and 3 work; MCP exposes ordinal display selection and exact display geometry; an agent can place one surface on the left while preserving an ops view on the right; commands are deterministic, revision-aware, validated, and covered by tests.
notes: Implemented and live-proved a stable full-desktop coordinate space with independent host windows, Ctrl-0..3 display selection, ordinal DisplayTarget over the socket/MCP, and canvas_place_surface with revision checks, coarse regions, margins, automatic display reveal, and preservation of unrelated placements. Live proof placed computing-mesh-design.md on display 1 while the six-surface ops board stayed on display 3; middle display remained normal macOS. Focused tests and strict Clippy pass.
close_reason: Implemented, tested, deployed, and live-proved Ctrl-0..3 selection, non-contiguous displays, ordinal MCP targeting, and revisioned screen-aware surface placement preserving unrelated views.

title: Build the Canvas operational widget primitive suite
description: Create high-quality native Canvas building blocks for Prometheus/Grafana-style read-only operational views. Cover the useful vocabulary rather than copying Grafana screens: stat/value, time series, gauge, bar gauge/VU, status/alert, table, histogram/heatmap, logs/events, and node/DAG summaries. Every primitive consumes bounded typed data and Coherence semantic palette roles, supports dark/light/project themes, and composes into a saved widget board.
design: Use a dense instrument-panel language: deep semantic surfaces, hairline borders, left-aligned labels/values, readable units and freshness, reserved success/warning/danger state, and motion only for meaningful live changes. Keep the renderer native iced/wgpu. Add per-surface chrome mode so operational widgets can use a quiet draggable strip without close/minimize/maximize dots while retaining move/resize semantics. Connector I/O remains outside widget renderers.
acceptance_criteria: Native production renderers exist for stat, time series, gauge, bar/VU meter, status/alert, table, histogram/heatmap, event/log, and node summary specs; malformed or unbounded data fails validation; all colors derive from ThemePalette; dark and light fixtures render legibly; a surface can select standard or drag-only chrome and hit testing matches visible controls; a representative ops board is live-tested and visually reviewed.
notes: Implemented and deployed typed stat, time-series, histogram, table, event-log, and node-summary widgets plus upgraded clock/ticker/gauge/meter/status presentation. Added drag-only chrome. Fixed the observed 50% content bug: center_y(Length::Fill) made the 26px drag strip consume half the surface; align_y now keeps it fixed-height. Live ops board was migrated and saved on the right monitor. Heatmap and further visual refinement remain.

title: Prove operational views with Prometheus and owner SSE connectors
description: Implement initial read-only connector adapters using the dock-cov.3 contract: Prometheus instant/range queries and authenticated ordered SSE feeds from Elmer's or MCP Bridge. Feed their typed outputs into retained Lua/widget scenes so Canvas can render gauges, time series, firing graphs, and DAG activity without a separate Grafana or source-specific UI. Ship a project-scoped saved operational-view fixture that JARVIS can later activate by exact project/view identity.
design: Prometheus and SSE network/auth logic stays in Rust owner adapters. Persist connector/query identities and view configuration, never bearer tokens or resolved endpoints. Apply bounded sample/event limits, replay cursors, cadence/backpressure, provenance, freshness and visible connector health. Lua transforms validated input only.
acceptance_criteria: A single saved project operational view combines at least one Prometheus query and one authenticated SSE stream; reconnect/replay and bounded backpressure are deterministic; stale or unauthorized sources are visibly degraded; no credentials enter JSON/Lua; one exact MCP intent activates the view idempotently; tests use production connector and shared-view paths.

title: Compose widgets into a chrome-light Canvas board
description: Canvas operational dashboards are saved, project-scoped, read-only views assembled from live or static sources. They replace rigid app-specific/Grafana-style dashboards with dynamically reconfigurable shared view state. JARVIS owns presence, alerts, and conversational intent; when the user says 'show me', the resolved intent identifies an exact project and saved view. Canvas deterministically switches project workspace, activates or reconstructs that view, and presents it. The first widget board should prove this contract: one persisted shared surface, multiple child widgets without per-widget chrome, useful default layout, and one idempotent MCP call.
acceptance_criteria: One MCP call creates or updates a single persisted project-scoped read-only operational view with clock, ticker, gauge, VU/status, and a richer chart; child widgets do not receive separate application title bars; default layout is useful on first open; repeated calls converge without duplicates; restart and workspace switching preserve the saved view; the response identifies the exact project/view state JARVIS can later activate after an alert.

title: Render shared views offscreen for headless agent vision
description: Add a renderer-neutral capture backend that renders an exact SharedViewDocument revision into an offscreen GPU texture and returns it through canvas_view_capture without depending on a visible compositor. Reuse the same scene/view renderer and source positions used by physical Canvas windows so desktop, Agora headless Sway, and future 3D viewers share one visual contract.
acceptance_criteria: The same shared-view revision renders through visible and offscreen targets; canvas_view_capture returns metadata and an encoded image without screencapture/grim; capture works without a visible host window on a supported Linux GPU node; image and PDF fixtures match visible geometry within an explicit tolerance; dimensions, GPU memory, render time, and encoded output are bounded; stale view revisions fail before rendering.

title: Open WidgetKind so a kind can be defined outside the Rust enum
description:
Load-bearing for everything below it, and a persistence one-way door, so worth doing deliberately.

Today crates/dock-widgets/src/lib.rs:56 declares WidgetKind as a closed Rust enum, serde(tag = 'kind', deny_unknown_fields), flattened into WidgetSpec. A new kind is therefore a new variant: Rust change, rebuild, deploy. An unrecognised kind does not degrade, it fails to parse.

Change: keep the seven built-ins as fast paths, add a variant carrying a module reference plus opaque params, validated against the module manifest's declared inputs rather than against Rust. WidgetSpec already has schema_version, unused so far, which is the migration handle for this.

The contraction argument matters as much as the expansion one. Consolidating two kinds later means migrating every instance that used them. If instances are declarative specs that is a mechanical rewrite over the corpus; if kinds stay hand-written Rust or hand-written modules, consolidation never happens. See dock-cov.11.

Reconcile two clocks while here: WidgetSpec.refresh_ms is a polling hint ('Refresh hint for live data in milliseconds'), while Lua modules animate on ModuleEvent::Pulse { sequence, delta_ms }, which is deterministic because the scheduler supplies time and scripts cannot read a clock. Animated widget specs should ride Pulse and refresh_ms should mean data staleness only, or agent-authored animation stops being replayable.

title: Place and store widget instances with the kinds we already have
description:
The usable flow first, before any new kinds exist. crates/dock-widgets already ships seven validated kinds (clock, ticker, gauge, meter, chart, status, text) and two render paths: live iced surfaces in-canvas, and external-tool PNG through plotters/matplotlib/doc-forge.

What is missing is the loop around them: create an instance, place it on a canvas surface, have it survive a restart, and find it again. A WidgetSpec is durable JSON by design ('Durable widget description. Serializes to JSON; both live and static renderers consume the same model') but nothing owns where instances live or how they are addressed.

Scope: instance storage and addressing, placement on a surface, reload, and removal. Reuse the Canvas view/revision model rather than inventing a second one - view state persistence is dock-cov.7 and instances should ride it, not parallel it.

Explicitly out of scope: new kinds, Lua, MCP. This is proving the flow is good with what exists.

Bound before this is reachable by an agent: WidgetSpec::Chart takes source: PathBuf and renderer Matplotlib shells out to python. An instance is only 'just data' once the path is constrained to a sanctioned directory and the renderer set is gated. Today an instance is a broader capability than a sandboxed Lua module.

title: Persist portable Canvas state and hand it across authenticated devices
description: Make shared views and workspaces reconstructible on another authenticated Canvas node without copying local GPU/window/credential state. Store validated compact JSON snapshots plus ordered JSONL patch and receipt journals.
design: Snapshots are the current source of truth; JSONL is an append-only bounded revision journal with compaction, conflict detection and provenance. Sync portable documents, Lua/template versions and immutable asset references. Each destination re-resolves authorization, source adapters, display topology and device capabilities locally.
acceptance_criteria: An authenticated second node reconstructs a workspace and exact shared view from snapshot+journal, rejects missing authorization and revision gaps, adapts layout to its displays without changing portable state, and records an acknowledged handoff. Tests cover compaction, replay, conflicts, offline edits and missing assets.

title: Prove the view language with Elmer's and MCP activity streams
description: Build the first complete multi-source live visualization: Elmer's brain topology/events and MCP tool firing feed one coherent retained graph view. The same reference should generalize to Edgerunner agent DAGs and other graph event streams.
design: Use exact source contracts and ordered sequences through the shared source adapter. Compose sources by stable node/edge IDs. Lua controls bounded visual adaptation and activity animation; Rust owns subscription, sequencing, view state, scheduling and rendering. Include provenance and legends.
acceptance_criteria: A live fixture and then the real authorized Elmer's/MCP streams render one graph with visible firing, source provenance, legends, selection and replay/hold behavior; gaps and schema drift fail visibly; static topology idles between events; the agent can focus a node and the user sees the same attention state.
notes:
Producer half of the MCP side now exists. shared-infra 0c4810e gives the MCP bridge GET /events over the same envelope Elmers has shipped since src/serve/brain.rs, and shared-infra docs/activity-stream.md writes that contract down so Canvas can adapt one source contract rather than one per service.

Frame shape: id: <seq> / event: call / data: {v,type,seq,at,data{connector,tool,client,auth_method,outcome,ms}}. Required hello and ping kinds; seq is gap detection and explicitly not a resume cursor since nothing is buffered.

Deliberately carries no payloads - identifiers, outcome and duration only. Enough to light a node up; anything more is behind an authorized route. A test drives a real call with a secret in its arguments and fails if it reaches the wire.

Note for this bead: the contract says seq is not resumable, while docs/canvas-shared-visualization.md describes holding a view 'at a replayable sequence'. Not incompatible - Canvas can hold a position it already received - but if Canvas is meant to re-request from a sequence, the contract needs to say who buffers and how far back. Cheap to settle now.

Not deployed: the bridge build on Batty still 404s on /events and /metrics until Fab ships it.

title: Move Lua side effects behind declared host adapters
description: The current Lua widget/event API exposes host clock access, synthetic stock data and direct curl execution despite the module manifest having no matching capabilities. This conflicts with the shared visualization boundary where source owners handle I/O and Lua receives bounded typed inputs.
design: Preserve event/webhook functionality by having Lua emit a declarative bounded event to a Rust-owned sink with explicit grants. Supply time and market data as declared input contracts. Lua must never spawn curl or invent source values.
acceptance_criteria: Lua cannot directly access the clock, network or process runner; time and price examples consume declared host inputs; webhook/event behavior is retained through an explicit allowlisted host sink; manifests and tests prove absent capabilities fail visibly.

title: Compose multi-source graph views through retained Lua
description: Connect keyed SharedViewDocument sources to the capability-scoped Lua module input boundary so a small adapter can visualize equivalent data from several owners in one coherent graph, including an Elmer's-style live firing view.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture combines at least two source owners into one graph view; bounded Lua maps typed snapshots/events to a retained scene without owning transport or GPU resources; theme, legends, source provenance and live activity are visible; hot reload and malformed input preserve the last known-good scene.

title: Normalize snapshots and streams behind typed Canvas connectors
description: Define the narrow connector interface for Canvas read-only visualization. A connector resolves an authorized named source owned elsewhere (Prometheus query/range data, SSE from Elmer's or MCP Bridge, finite artifacts, and later domain systems) and emits bounded typed snapshots or ordered events into the shared view lifecycle. Canvas owns view state and rendering; Rust host adapters own transport, credentials, reconnect/replay, rate limits, and schema validation; capability-scoped Lua receives only declared typed inputs and maps them into retained visual scenes. This is the substrate for project-scoped saved operational views, replacing fixed Grafana/app dashboards with the user's unified Canvas UI.
design: Connector identity is durable and machine-readable: owner, connector kind, source/query id, output contract, and position/cursor. Endpoint URLs and credentials remain host-local. All connectors normalize into snapshot or ordered-stream envelopes with timestamps/sequences, provenance, health, and explicit failure. Lua cannot perform I/O. Reconfiguration is a revisioned view change; repeated activation converges deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: One finite snapshot and replayable SSE fixture feed SharedViewDocument bindings through the same connector lifecycle; a connector registry resolves exact authorized identities without persisting secrets; gaps, duplicate sequences, schema mismatch, overflow, disconnect and stale data fail visibly or reconcile deterministically; idle static views request no frames; saved views can be reconstructed from connector identities on restart.

title: Persist Canvas display policy and load it through Lua
description: Canvas display targets and overlay anchors are typed socket/MCP state, but the live all-monitor target must currently be resent after restart and there is no direct Lua configuration loader. Add one durable policy source that Lua can author and the runtime can validate/reload without duplicating placement logic.
design: Keep DisplayTarget and OverlaySettings as the canonical runtime contract. Add a narrow validated Lua-to-policy adapter and persist the accepted policy through the existing workspace/runtime state boundary. Reject invalid monitor identities or overlay anchors loudly; resolve role targets such as leftmost/center/rightmost from live topology.
acceptance_criteria: After setting the display target and overlays through Lua, restarting Canvas restores the policy; socket/MCP inspection reports the resolved state; invalid Lua fails visibly without silently reverting; tests cover round-trip persistence, role resolution after topology changes, and invalid policy.

title: Preserve Canvas size while moving off-screen
description: Dragging a Canvas surface past a desktop edge is converted back to normalized workspace coordinates by clamping its position and shortening its extent, so a move appears as live resizing. Preserve translated geometry while retaining the interaction engine's reachable top-bar constraint.
acceptance_criteria: Top-bar drags preserve surface width and height when moved partially beyond the left or right workspace edge. Edge and corner drags continue to resize. Stored offscreen bounds remain valid and round-trip through visible geometry. Regression tests cover the conversion.
notes: Fixed the live move path in normalize_visible_surface_bounds: horizontal origins remain offscreen-capable and width/height no longer shrink to the desktop boundary. Added an offscreen geometry round-trip regression. Validation: 109 dock-canvas tests pass; dock-canvas all-target strict Clippy passes; managed right-monitor LaunchAgent restarted cleanly and restored Dock at 3840,0 1920x1200 with two surfaces. Workspace-wide fmt/build are currently blocked by unrelated uncommitted dock-widgets parser errors in the shared worktree and were left untouched.
close_reason: Preserved translated offscreen position and size through normalized workspace storage, retained reachable top-bar constraints, added regression coverage, and deployed the fix to the managed Canvas runtime.

title: Keep Canvas window top bars reachable while allowing off-screen content
description: Canvas currently clamps the entire surface inside the workspace. A user should be able to drag content beyond an edge, as on macOS, while the top bar remains sufficiently visible to recover the window.
design: Apply a reachability constraint only to move gestures: retain a bounded horizontal grab segment and the complete draggable top-bar height inside the workspace, while allowing the body and remaining width to extend past edges. Keep resize constraints and minimum sizes unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A moved surface can extend beyond every workspace edge, but cannot leave its complete top bar inaccessible; the retained grab width is deterministic and bounded; resize still enforces minimum size and usable bounds; tests cover all edges, oversized windows, and recovery drags.
close_reason: Move gestures now allow off-screen content while retaining a deterministic 72px reachable top-bar segment; resize bounds remain unchanged and tests cover both horizontal extremes and bottom overflow.

title: Show directional resize cursors on Canvas surface edges
description: Canvas resize handles work, but hover does not change the pointer to the horizontal, vertical, or diagonal resize cursor that corresponds to the drag action. Users cannot see which resize operation will begin before pressing.
design: Derive cursor shape from the same renderer-neutral hit-test result used to begin resize. Map left/right to horizontal, top/bottom to vertical, and corners to the two diagonal variants. Preserve pointer/tooltip behavior for window controls and ordinary content.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering each edge and corner produces the matching native resize cursor; moving into content restores the default pointer; the cursor mapping and resize hit target share one source of truth; tests cover all eight handles and non-resize regions.
close_reason: Directional cursors now derive from the shared resize hit test for every edge and corner; package tests and live deployment passed.

title: Resolve Canvas project identities and presentation targets through Alfalfa
description: Canvas must treat each Alfalfa project as a complete swappable desktop, not a nested window. Resolve project labels and resources from Alfalfa, expose deterministic list/switch/save intent through Canvas MCP and fpl-mcp, and keep host-local monitor assignments separate from portable workspace documents.
acceptance_criteria: An MCP intent can list and switch exact Alfalfa projects including Ohm; switching restores each full desktop without closing other project windows; snapshots expose project label and surface count; a host-local target can assign the desktop to one or multiple monitors; tests cover ambiguity, unknown projects, recall, and monitor target resolution.
notes: 2026-09-08: Shipped bounded Alfalfa-to-Canvas catalog sync through dock-mac MCP. Live sync created 379 missing desktops and preserved Dock for 380 total. canvas_workspace_switch recalled exact gh-1288853134 (ohmOS) and returned to Dock; snapshots expose label, status, surface count, active state, theme and background. Sync is atomic and preserves existing workspace documents. Remaining acceptance is an MCP host-local target contract for one or multiple monitors plus its target-resolution tests.

title: Make Canvas project workspaces durable and multi-display aware
description: Canvas already treats WorkspaceDocument as a full desktop, but its named workspace registry is process-local and arbitrary names obscure the project identity. A restart loses saved work and a project jump cannot yet prove that all surface context returns across the assigned display span.
design: Use project_id as the stable workspace identity and persist validated WorkspaceDocuments in an atomic local store owned by dock-canvas. Switching saves the outgoing project workspace automatically, loads the requested project document, and rehydrates durable surface types without closing the other project state. Keep the active display frame as runtime and presence placement so one workspace can be presented on one or several monitors without storing host-specific coordinates in portable project data. Expose exact project labels and surface counts through the socket and MCP snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: Dock and Ohm workspace documents survive Canvas restart, list by exact project ID, and swap without losing their respective surfaces, placements, focus, background, chrome, or spacing. The same document lays out over a one-display or multi-display runtime frame. Save and switch operations are atomic and revision checked; corrupted state fails loudly. Tests cover persistence, automatic outgoing save, recall, and project labels.
notes:
Core slice shipped in commits 8855c62 and e68fecf: exact project_id keyed atomic persistence, automatic outgoing checkpoint, restart recall, runtime-only display frame, and tests. Remaining: source dynamic project identities (including Ohm) from Alfalfa, expose labeled workspace summaries/surface counts through Canvas MCP/fpl-mcp, and persist host-local per-project monitor assignment.
Startup recall fixed and deployed in 90b14d2; the stored Dock desktop now loads immediately with its saved surface after process restart.

title: Reserve Canvas chrome space and expose workspace spacing
description: Surface controls currently overlay content, and the full Canvas workspace has no configurable outer padding or inter-surface gap, so content is obscured and the workspace background cannot remain visible. The Canvas workspace is the entire assigned multi-monitor desktop; spacing applies to surfaces within that desktop, never to a nested workspace window.
design: Make the toolbar a real layout strip above content. Add bounded canvas_padding and surface_gap fields to the existing workspace-owned SurfaceChrome policy. Derive rendered and interactive surface rectangles through one geometry helper, and invert that transform when direct manipulation writes normalized placements so drag/resize does not drift.
acceptance_criteria: Toolbar controls never cover surface content. Configurable padding reveals the background around the Canvas and configurable gaps separate adjacent surfaces. Rendering, control hit testing, focus, drag, and resize agree on visible geometry. Defaults are backward compatible and tests cover bounds transforms and serialization.
close_reason: Shipped reserved toolbar layout plus workspace-level surface padding/gaps with shared render and interaction geometry.

title: Make Canvas window chrome self-explanatory and reversible
description: Canvas maximize is one-way from the pointer controls, the three compact controls have no hover explanation, and surfaces cannot optionally show their title. These gaps make direct window management hard to discover and recover from.
design: Toggle maximized membership so the preserved placement becomes visible again. Give every compact control a pointer hover label while retaining its stable hit region. Add one workspace-owned chrome policy for surface titles with hidden, focused, and always modes; default to focused so the selected surface is identifiable without restoring full permanent title strips.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking maximize twice restores the exact previous placement. Hovering close, minimize, or maximize/restore identifies the pending action. Focused-title mode labels only the focused surface; hidden and always modes are deterministic and serializable. Tests cover toggle restoration, hover action resolution, backward-compatible chrome defaults, and all title modes.
close_reason: Shipped reversible maximize, control hover affordances, configurable title modes, and tests.

title: Build useful themed Canvas chart surfaces
description: The current DataViz surface renders one unlabeled x/y series with two axis lines. It cannot communicate what the data means or support practical financial, operational, or status views.
design: Define a renderer-neutral chart document with titled axes, units, named series, legend placement, chart kind, and bounded points. Parse useful CSV/TSV/JSON shapes into that contract. Render responsive axes, ticks, labels, legends, empty/error states, and pointer hover values using Coherence theme roles. Evaluate permissively licensed Rust chart crates, but keep the typed Canvas chart contract as the durable boundary and adopt a dependency only if it improves rendering without taking over Canvas state or theming.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-series chart displays a readable title, labeled axes with ticks, units, a legend, and theme-derived series colors at wide and narrow surface sizes. Pointer hover identifies the nearest point. Invalid/ambiguous input fails loudly. Tests cover parsing, bounds, tick calculation, legend layout, resize behavior, and empty/partial series.
close_reason: Shipped typed multi-series charts with axes, units, legends, responsive layout, hover values, parsing validation, and tests.

title: Pin one calm background family per Canvas workspace
description: Canvas privacy presentation currently rotates shader families every 45 seconds, making the desktop visually unstable. Keep the selected visual family stable for the active workspace and allow only bounded, slow motion within it. Workspace switches may select a different deterministic family; ordinary frame updates must not.
design: Use workspace identity and its Background state as the source of truth. Resolve one shader index when a workspace/document becomes active, keep elapsed animation local to that shader, and remove time-driven family rotation. Preserve explicit socket shader selection until the workspace changes. Keep screensaver privacy policy separate from normal workspace background rendering.
acceptance_criteria: A workspace retains one background/shader family indefinitely while active. Switching away and back resolves the same family. Explicit selection is stable. Tests prove elapsed time never changes shader index, workspace identity maps deterministically, and background animation stays frame-rate bounded.
close_reason: Shipped stable deterministic per-workspace background selection with bounded animation and tests.

title: Make nested Canvas resizing content-aware
description: Resizing an outer Canvas surface currently feels disconnected from the renderer inside it. Child canvases and media keep stale or independent viewport assumptions, and body gestures compete with embedded content interaction.
design: Treat the current placement bounds as the single logical viewport supplied to the child renderer. Reflow native scenes, terminals, charts, and documents to that viewport; preserve source aspect only for media whose fit policy requests it. Reserve the top chrome as the window move region, keep edges/corners for resize, and let content-body pointer input reach the child after focus/front promotion.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a surface edge or corner updates outer bounds and the child viewport together in the same frame. Charts and other native Canvas content reflow; images/video honor explicit contain/cover behavior without controlling the outer window aspect. Pointer presses in content focus/promote without beginning a window move, while top-bar drags move and edge drags resize. Tests cover nested viewport propagation, aspect policy, input-region routing, and resize convergence.
close_reason: Placement bounds now drive nested scene viewport; native surfaces fill/reflow, media preserves explicit fit, and content/top-bar/edge input regions are separated and tested.

title: Make Canvas surfaces discoverable and restorable
description: Canvas surfaces need restrained visible edges and top chrome, a user-operated dock for minimized surfaces, and reliable click-to-front behavior. Today minimized surfaces disappear with no direct recovery affordance and live selection does not visibly promote overlap order.
design: Keep WorkspaceDocument layout and InteractionEngine as the authoritative state. Render one coherent surface chrome treatment and a bottom overlay derived from minimized surface IDs. Restoring, focusing, and promoting must mutate the existing state path; do not create a second window manager or separate z-order store.
acceptance_criteria: Every visible surface has a clear edge and usable top drag region without persistent labels. Minimized surfaces appear in a bottom dock and restore by pointer click. Clicking any exposed part of a surface focuses it and raises it above overlapping peers. Socket actions and pointer actions converge on the same state. Tests cover minimize/restore discovery, overlap promotion, hit geometry, and empty dock behavior.
close_reason: Implemented visible surface chrome, pointer focus/front promotion, minimized dock restore flow, and regression tests.

title: Make Canvas backgrounds configurable workspace state
description: Add a first-class Canvas background layer that is part of machine-readable workspace intent and can be selected per project. Support theme-derived or explicit solid colors, typed gradients, managed images with fit behavior, and named animated shader scenes. The same validated contract must drive native Mac, Linux/WebGPU, socket, MCP, persistence, and workspace reconciliation without embedding host paths or arbitrary shader source in workspace documents.
design: Define one versioned Background contract in dock-canvas and reference managed assets and a bounded built-in shader registry by stable IDs. Keep rendering behind a narrow backend-independent interface. Static gradients should render without a frame loop; animated shaders request frames only while visible. Preserve the existing screensaver renderer by adapting it to named shader backgrounds and later presence privacy policy. Background changes are normal deterministic document patches and must survive inspect, serialize, restore, and project recall.
acceptance_criteria: WorkspaceDocument carries a validated configurable background with backward-compatible default. Solid, gradient, managed-image and named-shader variants round-trip through JSON/MCP, reject invalid colors/stops/asset references/shader IDs, and participate in deterministic reconciliation. Canvas visibly renders each type as the bottom layer with no margins. Socket/MCP can change it using revision checks. Tests cover validation, patching, persistence, no-op convergence, and frame scheduling for static versus animated backgrounds.

title: Render zone-aware presence in Canvas
description: Canvas needs a subtle, generic presence surface: a persistent zone label, bounded multi-person rows, independent Presence/Face/Voice evidence colors, and a transient recognition panel that can show a supplied in-memory face preview without turning Canvas into an identity authority.
design: Add a versioned generic Canvas control command and state. Keep the compact presence strip persistent at the bottom edge, render each person once with three evidence channels, and show face imagery only as a short-lived recognition moment. Canvas owns layout and animation; publishers own identity semantics and expiry. Missing/stale evidence must remain visibly unknown.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas validates and renders a bounded zone presence snapshot with multiple occupants and separate presence, face, and voice evidence. The configured zone name remains subtly visible at the bottom. A transient preview with face bounds and display name renders without blocking other Canvas or audio work and expires automatically. Tests cover malformed, stale, unknown, and multiple-person payloads.

title: Replace Canvas surface title strips with minimal overlay controls
description: The first surface chrome consumes content height, repeats labels, and renders oversized rectangular controls on the right. Replace the strip with small coherent controls overlaid on content so Canvas still feels like one seamless desktop.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas surfaces render at full height with no persistent title strip or repeated label. Close, minimize, and maximize remain reachable through stable upper-left hit targets, while body drag and edge resize continue to work. Tests verify control ordering and hit bounds, and a live capture confirms the corrected presentation.
notes:
Implemented in the validated staged Canvas: removed the 28px labeled title strip; content now fills each surface; close/minimize/maximize are 9px semantic-color circles overlaid at upper left with independent 18px hit targets. Added a hit-order/bounds regression test and deployed the staged binary to the existing DockCanvas.app LaunchAgent. Native capture currently reports sharing state 0, so automated screenshot validation cannot see the Canvas window even though its socket and two live surfaces are healthy.
Second chrome pass shipped in b52591c and 0bbd1fe: Canvas now uses the complete macOS display frame (3840,0 1920x1200 on the right monitor, instead of visible_frame at y=25/1175px high) and requests app-scoped auto-hide for the macOS menu bar and Dock. Focused tests and strict all-target/all-feature Clippy pass. Live launch reports the exact full frame, and a display capture confirms the 25px system bar is gone; Canvas content itself is still omitted from automated capture because macOS reports sharing state 0.
close_reason: Removed persistent surface title strips, retained compact overlay controls and hit targets, expanded Canvas to the complete display frame, and auto-hide macOS menu/Dock chrome. Focused tests, strict Clippy, live full-frame inspection, and display capture verification pass; Canvas capture-sharing remains separately tracked in dock-2kf.9.15.

title: Terminal surface: PTY-backed shell inside Canvas
description: Add a terminal surface type that renders a PTY-backed shell inside the Canvas. Uses posix_openpt/forkpty via libc (already a dependency). SurfaceContent::Terminal is defined in the document model but not rendered yet. The terminal should: spawn a shell in a PTY, capture output as styled text (VT100 parsing), render via iced text widget, accept keyboard input from the Canvas event loop. Integrates with the title bar (close/minimize/maximize buttons) and tiling system.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reconcile high-level workspace intent into deterministic Canvas state
description: Expose intent-level MCP tools for requests such as bring up the Ohm workspace, show FPL in Dock, or open last week’s invoice for a named customer. The LLM resolves ambiguous language into typed project, resource, and presentation intent. A deterministic reconciler then reads the authoritative Canvas document and catalog, computes the smallest validated patch needed to reach that desired state, applies it through the owner-local revisioned socket, and returns a receipt. Keep identity and resource search in Alfalfa, workspace policy in Dock, rendering in Canvas, and transport in the raw socket.
design: Define a versioned DesiredWorkspaceState contract separately from imperative socket commands. Reconciliation is a pure current-state plus desired-state to patch calculation with stable ordering, explicit conflicts, dry-run/explain output, revision checks, and idempotent convergence. Never ask the LLM to infer pixel operations or blindly retry stale mutations. Asset resolution produces exact authorized resource references before reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: MCP can express project recall, exact resource reveal, focus, visibility, and layout intent without embedding raw socket commands. Unit tests prove no-op convergence, minimal patches, stable ordering, conflict handling, missing/ambiguous resource failures, and preservation of unrelated human-arranged surfaces. An end-to-end test resolves and applies representative Ohm workspace, FPL Dock, and prior-invoice intents through the existing socket with machine-readable receipts.
notes: Implemented first deterministic intent slice in commit 8524620: versioned DesiredWorkspaceState, pure stable reconciler, no-op/minimal patch/exact replacement actions, preservation and exact modes, explicit focus, catalog validation, self-validation, dry-run change receipts, and canvas_reconcile_intent MCP inspect-reconcile-apply flow with runtime revision checks. Added 7 focused tests including mocked socket application for an invoice reveal and exact Ohm project recall coverage. Full workspace all-feature tests pass (186 passed, 4 intentional live-desktop ignores); workspace build and strict all-target/all-feature Clippy pass. Alfalfa-side natural-language/asset resolver integration and representative live FPL/Ohm/invoice scenarios remain before closing.

title: Launch Canvas as a visible macOS application
description: The direct Canvas executable can create a window from a LaunchAgent but macOS leaves it on a non-current Space and NSRunningApplication cannot activate it. Add a minimal signed app-bundle packaging path so the runtime can launch through LaunchServices and remain visible on its configured display.
acceptance_criteria: A packaged DockCanvas.app launches through LaunchServices as one process, owns the Canvas socket, and its main window is visible on the configured display. The Rust Canvas runtime remains cross-platform; packaging is only the macOS adapter.
notes: 2026-09-07: Packaged Canvas launches under the existing KeepAlive LaunchAgent and the socket remains healthy after replacement. CGWindow reports the 1920x1175 right-display window on screen but sharing state remains 0 after NSWindowSharingReadOnly, so screencapture omits it. Investigate capture behavior separately from launch visibility.
close_reason: Canvas now packages as a signed macOS app and launches visibly through a single-instance LaunchServices LaunchAgent; live job and screenshot verified.

title: Add caption and optional diagnostics to Canvas indicators
description: Extend Canvas transient status indicators with bounded generic detail and diagnostic text so JARVIS can restore user/assistant captions and opt-in voice-loop telemetry without owning a separate window.
design: Keep the Canvas protocol generic: caption, detail, and diagnostic are optional bounded strings. Canvas owns layout. Normal indicators show caption/detail when supplied; diagnostic telemetry is supplied only when the client configuration opts in. Preserve old clients that omit the new fields.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas accepts, validates, inspects, and renders bounded caption/detail/diagnostic fields. Missing fields remain compatible. Tests cover limits and wire compatibility. JARVIS captions appear during a live turn; diagnostics remain disabled by default and can be enabled in configuration.
close_reason: Canvas protocol and indicator renderer now support bounded caption, assistant detail, and optional diagnostics; protocol tests and screenshots verified.

title: Mermaid diagram rendering in Markdown surfaces
description: Support Mermaid.js diagram syntax inside Markdown code blocks. When the canvas Markdown renderer encounters a mermaid code fence, it should render the diagram and embed it alongside the text. Approaches: 1) use the mmdc CLI to convert to SVG/PNG then render as an image surface, 2) parse common Mermaid diagram types (flowchart, sequence, gantt, class, state) natively in Rust for offline use. Mermaid is widely used for architecture diagrams, state machines, timelines, and entity relationships - core to our workflow.
notes: Partial milestone: typed canvas_mermaid MCP tool renders bounded Mermaid source through mmdc outside Canvas and opens the result through the native content loader. Inline detection/replacement of mermaid fences inside Markdown surfaces remains open.
close_reason: Closed

title: Raw stream windows (NVR/camera feeds)
description: Bring in raw video streams (RTSP, NVR, WebRTC) as canvas surfaces. The canvas already handles raster media — extend it to decode live video streams. Use the existing media backend infrastructure (media.rs, backend.rs) to manage stream lifecycle (connect, reconnect, suspend when off-screen). Need a StreamSource/StreamSurface content type.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bind Hyperspace as a native Canvas GPU backend
description: Integrate Hyperspace as a specialized VisualBackend that renders directly into Canvas' iced/wgpu compositor. Preserve Hyperspace scene and shader ownership; Canvas supplies lifecycle, placement, input, timing, and a target texture. Avoid subprocess video encoding and CPU framebuffer readback.
design: Use iced_wgpu's custom Primitive/Pipeline hook, which exposes the compositor's wgpu Device, Queue, target format, command encoder, and TextureView. Align Hyperspace and Dock on one wgpu major (currently Hyperspace feat/wav-to-mp4-render uses wgpu 25 while iced 0.14 resolves wgpu 27). Evolve Hyperspace ScopeRenderer from per-pass queue.submit calls to encode all scene, post, and blit passes into the host frame command encoder. Define only a narrow GPU frame contract: size/scale, target format/color space/alpha, load/blend behavior, timing, resource generation, resize/suspend, and device-loss recovery. Do not share Canvas documents, map semantics, credentials, or domain state with Hyperspace. Keep it optional and fail loudly on incompatible GPU capabilities. Resolve AGPL/proprietary distribution compatibility before shipping a direct crate dependency; dual-license/relicense owned code or retain a process boundary if required.
acceptance_criteria: A Hyperspace scene renders inside a clipped, resizable native Canvas surface using Canvas' wgpu device with no CPU readback and no intermediate encoded video. One host frame submission contains the Hyperspace main/post/blit work; resize, pause/resume, device loss, reduced motion, and surface removal are deterministic. Measured p95/p99 GPU and frame timing are reported at 60/90/120 Hz targets, with bounded GPU memory and no render-thread file/network/audio decode. Tests reject target-format and lifecycle mismatches, and a license/packaging decision is documented before distribution.
notes: 2026-09-07 Hyperspace shader inventory: treat Hyperspace primarily as a specialized FX backend. Full scenes such as acid, nebula, gforce, oscilloscope, spectrum, tunnel, cyberpunk, point-cloud, and neural-link assume Hyperspace's audio/CV/state/feedback ABI and should remain owned there. Candidates for a small shared permissively-licensed FPL shader kit are palette/color-grade functions, hash/noise primitives, flow/UV warps, fullscreen blit, feedback/ping-pong helpers, easing, and selection/glow techniques. Extract source functions behind Canvas-owned bindings rather than importing Hyperspace's group-0 layout or scene uniforms. Keep post effects opt-in, bounded, reduced-motion aware, and visually subordinate to intelligence legibility.

title: Profile suspected Dock desktop memory growth
description: The owner observed that Dock may have a memory leak during the desktop/streaming work. Reproduce with a bounded soak across the Mac shell, Canvas, viewer, and control bridge; record resident/private/GPU memory by process and operation; identify retained resources or prove a stable plateau before changing code.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable soak script captures per-process CPU/RSS/private/GPU proxies over idle, repeated project recalls, media open/close, drag/resize, and streaming; results identify the leaking owner and trigger or show a stable plateau; any fix has a regression test or measurable before/after evidence.
notes: Captured from the user's earlier observation: 'Dock might have a memory leak.' No process has yet been proven responsible, so profile before patching.

title: Conky-style mesh HUD as Canvas overlay
description: Conky-style passive HUD overlay rendered in Canvas showing the computing mesh: which nodes are running (Agora, Mac, other nodes), each with state, plus local CPU/RAM/uptime on the primary node. Data comes from existing presence/owner status sources; Canvas subscribes and redraws on a timer tick. Design constraints: Coherence palette, strictly passive (no buttons - the button dashboard was rejected), reads at a glance from the VNC stream.
design: First cut: one gauge/panel surface in a corner of the primary output. Add a new ContentKind (e.g. gauge) or indicator variant to dock-canvas/src/control.rs; reuse lua_scene node system if a gauge node type fits. Must distinguish hidden UI vs paused agents vs stopped processes vs suspended compute per the pause/resume semantics tenet.
notes:
First cut complete and verified live (2026-09-07):
- SetMesh protocol in control.rs: MeshNodeState {active, paused, suspended, stopped, hidden} (pause/resume semantics kept distinct), bounded 8 nodes, MeshSet receipt, mesh carried in RuntimeSnapshot.
- Passive HUD in hud.rs: local hostname row + one row per mesh node with state colors drawn from the project ThemePalette, CPU/RAM arc gauges, uptime line. Top-right of the primary output, strictly no buttons.
- Local metrics via sysinfo 0.36, refreshed on a 2s tick (METRICS_REFRESH).
- Verified all five states rendering in a live capture: docs/screenshots/canvas-mesh-hud.png. 48/48 canvas tests green.
Remaining / follow-ups:
- Orchestrator-driven SetMesh publishing from the presence/owner status source (the Canvas currently just accepts pushes).
- HUD theming for imported-palette projects is blocked on the canvas project_theme() accepting ThemeSelection (currently Coherence-only).

title: Make Canvas control and rendering event-driven at interactive latency
description: Remove polling and redundant redraw/decode work from Canvas so agent-issued moves, workspace patches, and surface updates appear immediately while idle GPU/CPU use stays near zero. Introduce an event-driven socket-to-iced wake path, retained GPU resources, coalesced geometry updates, bounded media decode/upload queues, and frame-time/command-latency diagnostics.
design: Keep the socket protocol authoritative and deterministic. Transport wakes orchestration, orchestration prepares validated deltas off frame, and the renderer consumes compact retained changes at frame boundaries. Lua and external agents never issue raw GPU commands.
acceptance_criteria: Idle Canvas performs no continuous decorative redraw; local socket commands wake the runtime without polling and report end-to-end apply latency; geometry bursts coalesce without losing final state; textures and PDF pages reuse bounded caches; diagnostics expose decode, upload, apply, and present timing; representative interaction remains smooth at native monitor resolution.
notes:
User prioritized ricing first, then GPU/runtime speed and faster agent motion on 2026-09-07.
Live drag proof exposed a concrete coalescing target: motion samples each advance the durable document/runtime revision. Preserve responsive transient bounds during capture, then commit one authoritative bounds revision on release while retaining final-state determinism.

title: Build the Canvas Lua module SDK and GPU scene primitives
description: Create a capability-scoped mlua module system for small Canvas logic. Modules receive typed data and Coherence-derived theme tokens and emit retained, renderer-neutral scene primitives instead of owning the GPU or OS. Cover reusable graphs/P&L/status indicators plus typed media/map/video surfaces suitable for NVR streams and spatial placement. Keep module execution bounded, deterministic, hot-reloadable, and isolated behind the Canvas socket/runtime contract.
design: Lua controls bounded presentation logic only. The Rust host owns scheduling, validation, media ingest, textures, GPU resources, and external I/O. Modules exchange typed snapshots/events and retained scene descriptions so the same module can render in iced/wgpu, WebGPU, or a later LÖVR adapter.
acceptance_criteria: A documented and tested module lifecycle loads and reloads Lua safely; capability manifests gate filesystem/network/process access; Coherence tokens are supplied from the host; example modules cover a graph and status/P&L surface; scene/data contracts admit video/NVR and map surfaces without embedding vendor logic; per-frame Lua work is bounded and GPU resources remain host-owned.
notes: Implemented first Canvas Lua module SDK slice in lua_module.rs atop lua_scene.rs. Versioned deny-unknown manifest; explicit scene/input/theme/resource capabilities; typed serializable snapshots and events; Coherence-derived theme tokens; retained renderer-neutral output; monotonic update revisions; atomic last-known-good hot reload; bounded source/memory/interrupt/combined-node execution. title: Render transient status indicators in Canvas
description: Add a bounded transient status-indicator control primitive to the long-lived Canvas runtime so clients such as JARVIS can present lifecycle state without owning another OS window or rewriting the durable workspace document.
design: The control protocol carries semantic indicator state, not JARVIS pixels or arbitrary code. Canvas owns rendering and keeps transient indicators outside durable workspace state. Upsert by stable surface id is idempotent; dismiss removes it. Preserve the generic project workspace underneath.

title: Design the initial Canvas background and native view
description: Give the persistent Canvas runtime a fast, polished initial background, command-connected status, strong content framing, and project-derived visual identity suitable for the rightmost desktop display.

title: Render Canvas media at physical-pixel quality
description: Make image and PDF surfaces resolve against viewport logical size, display scale factor, source dimensions, and memory limits so Canvas does not upscale low-resolution rasters or retain blurry PDF pages after resize.
design: Introduce a renderer-neutral raster plan and cache key. Preserve 1:1 display for undersized raster sources, select physical-pixel PDF targets, rerasterize after meaningful viewport or scale changes, cap dimensions and allocations, and keep decode/upload off the render thread.

title: Build socket-driven Canvas runtime
description: Create a long-lived native Canvas process controlled through a private owner-local socket. Commands must inspect and mutate typed presentation state from startup: open bounded file/PDF content, move and resize the Canvas window, focus it, navigate content, apply project theme, set wallpaper through the platform adapter, and close content. The socket is the primary control interface for Dock, MCP, and JARVIS.
design: Keep the command protocol in dock-canvas and platform execution behind narrow adapters. Use an iced native window and asynchronous bounded file/PDF decode so the render thread never performs I/O or launches helpers. Authenticate Unix peers by owner UID, bound frames/messages/queues, make mutations revisioned/idempotent where applicable, and return receipts. Mac first; preserve the protocol for a Linux implementation and later Agora-rendered remote surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: A persistent Canvas process starts once and accepts multiple sequential authenticated socket commands without relaunch. Live proof opens a local image or PDF, reports state, changes page where applicable, moves/resizes/focuses its own window, applies a project theme, and sets a bounded wallpaper request through the Mac adapter. Invalid peers, malformed/oversized commands, stale revisions, unsupported files, and out-of-bounds geometry fail loudly. Tests cover protocol, framing, state transitions, and platform adapter boundaries; workspace quality gates pass.
